can_fail_a.instructions: Can breaking the named behaviour in the code under test make this test fail?

can_fail_b.instructions: Does this test pass however the code under test breaks the named behaviour?

can_fail_c.instructions: If the named behaviour regresses, can this test turn red?

asserts_a.instructions: Which assertion kind is the strongest assertion in this test?

criteria.behaviour: the output, against an expected value
criteria.hardcoded-data: a value from the code under test itself
criteria.shape-only: only type, length, keys, or presence
criteria.interaction-only: only a mock or spy call
criteria.nothing: nothing, a tautology, or only no throw

asserts_b.instructions: What does the strongest assertion check?

criteria.nothing: nothing, a tautology, or only no throw
criteria.interaction-only: only a mock or spy call
criteria.shape-only: only type, length, keys, or presence
criteria.hardcoded-data: a value from the code under test itself
criteria.behaviour: the output, against an expected value

positive_a.instructions: Does at least one assertion expect a non-empty value?

criteria.true: at least one expects a non-empty value
criteria.false: every assertion expects empty, null, undefined, or no throw

positive_b.instructions: Does every assertion expect only empty, null, undefined, or no throw?

criteria.true: every assertion expects empty, null, undefined, or no throw
criteria.false: at least one expects a non-empty value

runs_a.instructions: Does this test run, with no marker in the file narrowing the run?

criteria.true: it runs, and nothing narrows the run
criteria.false: a marker stops it or narrows the run

runs_b.instructions: Does a marker stop this test or narrow the run?

criteria.true: a marker stops it or narrows the run
criteria.false: it runs, and nothing narrows the run

type.instructions: What type of test is this?

criteria.unit: one unit, collaborators mocked or absent
criteria.regression: the name cites a past bug or issue
criteria.e2e: the whole system through its public interface
criteria.smoke: only that something runs or exists
criteria.characterization: pins current output before a change

conditional.instructions: Does every assertion in this test always run? Answer no when a branch, a loop over a value that may be empty, an early return, or a try/catch can leave an assertion unrun or swallow its failure.

criteria.false: a branch, loop, early return, or catch can leave an assertion unrun or swallow its failure

isolated.instructions: Does this test read only values that it builds itself, or that a hook in fixtures builds before each test? Answer no when it reads a value that another test must set, or mutable state in setup that is shared with other tests and that no hook resets. An object the file declares once, such as a registry, that this test reads but another test fills, is shared state.

criteria.true: it builds what it reads, so it passes alone and in any order
criteria.false: it reads state that another test sets, or mutable state shared with other tests

deterministic.instructions: Does this test give the same result on every run? It does not when it reads the real clock or real randomness, calls the network, waits on a sleep, or relies on an order nothing guarantees. A clock, timer, or random source that the test fakes or seeds is under its control and is fine.

criteria.true: the result is the same on every run of the same code
criteria.false: the result can differ between runs of the same code

automated.instructions: Does this test reach a pass or fail with no person doing or reading anything?

criteria.false: it has no assertion and only prints, or it waits for a person to act or to read its output

restores.instructions: Does the test leave every global, environment variable, timer, module mock, spy, and shared object that the file or its setup declares as it found them? A restore in an after hook in fixtures counts. A test that changes none of these counts as yes.

criteria.true: it changes none of these, or it restores what it changes
criteria.false: it leaves a global, environment variable, timer, mock, spy, or shared object changed

verdict.instructions: How strong a guard is this test: slop, weak, good, or strong?
